_note: The provenance of every captured artifact under tools/gates/fixtures. Written by hand, read by tools/gates/probes/readers.mjs (and by its `the captured fixtures are present` self-check in probes/_harness.mjs). Every entry says the exact command that produced the file and whether the bytes are VERBATIM output (real: true) or a named edit of real output (real: false, with `derivedFrom` and `edit`). A fixture nobody can re-capture is a fixture nobody can trust, so re-capture is the cure for a stale one — never a hand edit. No seconds figure is promised anywhere here; the `time`/`start_time` fields inside an artifact are that artifact's own content.

sources._note: sha256 of the committed test sources a fixture was captured FROM. A probe that compares a stored artifact against a live source reads these first and SKIPS with `re-capture` when they disagree — a stale fixture must never read as a defect in the reader.

vitest/core-skeleton.junit.xml.note: The committed tree's own core run: 17 cases over 2 files, all green. Carries the case `hashes "abc"` as `"abc"`, which is the XML side of the escaping measurement.

vitest/list-core.json.edit: the absolute `file` values were made repo-relative; every `name` is verbatim, INCLUDING the double-escaped quote (`hashes \"abc\"` after JSON.parse) that is the whole point of this fixture
vitest/list-core.json.note: The runner's own collection, the second enumerator. `name` is byte-identical to the JUnit `testcase name` only AFTER the backslash-escaped quote is unescaped — measured; the live absolute-path form is probed live, where it is honest.

vitest/all-failed.junit.xml.command: the same shape, over a file whose three cases fail differently
vitest/all-failed.junit.xml.note: The three measured red signatures in ONE artifact: AssertionError `expected '@cheq/core' to be '@cheq/nope'`, TypeError `completeTask is not a function`, ReferenceError `absentFn is not defined`. Exit 1.

vitest/skipped-only.junit.xml.command: the same shape, over a file with one it.skip and one it.todo
vitest/skipped-only.junit.xml.note: Two <testcase> elements, each with <skipped/>, suite skipped="2", failures="0" — and the run EXITS 0. The XML cannot tell .skip from .todo; the JSON channel can.

vitest/skipped-only.json.note: numPendingTests 1 + numTodoTests 1 = the XML's skipped 2 — the one place the distinction survives.

vitest/collection-failure.junit.xml.command: the same shape, over a file importing ../../src/scheduling/schedule.ts, which does not exist
vitest/collection-failure.junit.xml.note: MEASURED signature: classname="packages/core/test/__cap/collect.test.ts" (repo-relative) and name="test/__cap/collect.test.ts" (project-relative). They are NOT equal, and name is not the basename either; `classname.endsWith('/' + name)` is what fires.

vitest/collection-failure.json.note: MEASURED and previously unmeasured (TD-0005/TD-0012): numTotalTests 0, testResults[0] with status failed, a message, and assertionResults []. So the JSON channel of a run whose ONLY file failed to collect is itself CANNOT VERIFY by the numTotalTests rule.

vitest/empty-run.junit.xml.command: the same shape with --passWithNoTests=true and a filter matching nothing
vitest/empty-run.junit.xml.note: MEASURED: tests="0", a well-formed report, and the run EXITS 0. This is the silent green that `tests="0" ⇒ CANNOT VERIFY` exists for.

vitest/foreign-file.junit.xml.note: A real run of ANOTHER project: every classname is under apps/api. Asked about a core file, a reader must answer CANNOT VERIFY rather than reading somebody else's green.

vitest/counter-mismatch.junit.xml.note: The XML half of the disagreement pair: tests="1".

vitest/counter-mismatch.json.edit: numTotalTests and numPassedTests raised from 1 to 2
vitest/counter-mismatch.json.note: The toolchain has never been observed producing two channels that disagree (TD-0005), so this fixture is the ONLY way to exercise crossCheck's refusal. It is derived, and it says so.

tsc/core-clean.listfiles.log.note: Clean, 99 --listFiles lines. The lib files are under @typescript/typescript-<platform>/lib/, NOT node_modules/typescript/lib/ — the measured trap.

tsc/red-ts2322.listfiles.log.command: the same, over a scratch project with two deliberate assignment errors
tsc/red-ts2322.listfiles.log.note: Two `error TS2322` lines with RELATIVE paths, then 62 absolute --listFiles lines. Exit 1.

tsc/no-inputs-ts18003.log.command: the same, over a tsconfig whose include matches nothing
tsc/no-inputs-ts18003.log.note: One GLOBAL diagnostic with no file position: `error TS18003: No inputs were found in config file`. Exit 2. A configuration that did not load is red, not a clean project.

tsc/clean-without-listfiles.log.note: EMPTY, zero bytes, exit 0. The measured shape of `never ran is not green`: no diagnostics and no evidence the compiler read anything.

oxlint/clean.json.note: The lint lane green over this tree: number_of_files 49, number_of_rules 243, diagnostics [].

oxlint/findings.json.command: oxlint --format=json src  (in a scratch project with a debugger statement and an empty binding pattern)
oxlint/findings.json.note: Two diagnostics. `code` is `plugin(rule)` — `eslint(no-debugger)` — and the line/column live in labels[].span, not at the top level.

oxlint/zero-files.raw.json.note: MEASURED and not what the design assumed: stdout carries the PROSE line `No files found to lint. Please check your paths and ignore patterns.` BEFORE the JSON, and oxlint exits 1. Since the lint lane's artifact IS oxlint's stdout, the artifact of a zero-file run is not valid JSON at all.

oxlint/zero-files.derived.json.note: What the reader's `number_of_files === 0` branch was written against. It is reachable only when a caller strips the prose line, which nothing does today — the raw fixture is the honest one, and this one exists so that branch is still exercised.
